description: Collapse the three full test-suite executions inside one `bun run check:all` into a single captured `bun test --coverage` run that feeds the coverage and skip-ratchet gates in-process.

officialDocsConsulted.version: current (docs served for Bun 1.3.x; local runtime is Bun 1.3.13)
officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms the exact seam this PRD depends on: `Bun.spawnSync` returns a `SyncSubprocess` whose `stdout`/`stderr` are `Buffer | undefined` (not `ReadableStream`) and which carries `success` plus `exitCode`; per-stream options are `stdin`/`stdout`/`stderr` with values 'pipe' | 'inherit' | 'ignore'; 'pipe' is the default for stdout and 'inherit' the default for stderr, so BOTH streams must be set to 'pipe' explicitly to capture the suite blob. `maxBuffer` (spawnSync-only) caps captured bytes and kills the child when exceeded, so it must be left unset for a multi-hundred-KB coverage+summary blob. No deprecation or breaking change affecting this change.
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: This repo's gate spine spawns every gate with stdio fully inherited (`scripts/check-all.ts:131`, and the 'inherit','inherit' generics baked into `SpawnFn` at check-all.ts:34) precisely to keep the operator's live progress visible, while the official capture path requires 'pipe'; RESOLVED FOR THIS PRD in favour of the official pipe form for the suite gate only, with live progress restored by echoing the captured buffers back out after the spawn returns (see US-001 notes: no `tee`/shell form, because every downstream oracle in US-002 and US-003 injects the shared blob through the fake spawn's stdout/stderr Buffers).

userStories.title: CRITICAL: Layer B behavioral gate FAIL, independently reproduced at branch HEAD…
userStories.description: CRITICAL [scripts/cam/prd.json:60]: Layer B behavioral gate FAIL, independently reproduced at branch HEAD (064bb52b) by this reviewer in round 6. 8 recorded change-detection oracle directives print RED. Verbatim re-run: US-001 AC1 'RED suite='; US-001 AC3 'RED test=missing'; US-002 AC1 'RED suite=0 consumers=0'; US-002 AC2 'RED cov=missing suite=0 consumers=0'; US-002 AC3 'RED BAD status=missing suite=0 | BAD status=missing suite=0 | BAD status=missing suite=0'; US-002 AC4 'RED a=missing/missing/missing b=missing/missing'; US-002 AC5 'RED cov=missing sr=missing suite=0 consumers=0'; US-002 AC7 'RED keys= names='. Root cause verified in source: US-R2-001 made the spine async end to end (scripts/check-all.ts:63 SpawnFn returns a Promise; scripts/check-all.ts:407 runGates returns Promise<number>), but every one of these directives calls runGates({...}) WITHOUT await and reads its log/rows array on the very next synchronous statement, so it observes an empty array before any gate has run. Control proving the product itself is intact: the same directives rewritten with 'await runGates(...)' and an async fake spawnFn print GREEN, test/check-all-inprocess-gates.test.ts covers the same behaviour against the real manifest gates and passes, bun test is 5956 pass / 0 fail, and a real 'bun scripts/check-all.ts --json' is green on all 14 gates. This is a broken proof-of-record, not a broken feature, but these 8 criteria carry the entire anti-inert value of US-001/US-002 (one suite spawn, zero consumer spawns, exit-code fidelity, under-floor coverage fail, three skip-ratchet failure modes, anti-contamination, empty-blob fail-closed, gate identity) and read RED for the ship gate, for the next planner's red-against-main sweep, and for the next reviewer. Fix: restate the 8 directives against the async seam (await runGates(...) with an async fake spawnFn) and re-sweep them red-against-main. Include US-001 AC2 in the same restatement: it prints GREEN only incidentally. This reviewer re-captured its output and grepped it: the ONLY SENTINELOUT/SENTINELERR hit is line 17, the skip-ratchet failure message's 'Raw output (first 300 chars):' dump of the raw blob. After US-R2-001 no echo path exists for an injected fake at all (the tee lives in runStreamingSuiteGate, scripts/check-all.ts:276-298, reachable only via the default spawnFn at :392-398; runSpawnGate at :321-334 has no echo), so AC2 would stay green even if the tee were deleted entirely. Raised in rounds 3, 4 and 5; unaddressed at HEAD. Note: prd.json is write-blocked for worker-actor sessions by .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh, so this must land via a planner/reviewer/operator pass, not an implementer story.

userStories.title: WARNING: The suite gate produces NO output for its entire ~101s run, contradict…
userStories.description: WARNING [scripts/check-all.ts:224]: The suite gate produces NO output for its entire ~101s run, contradicting US-001's own AC2 prose ('the captured buffers are echoed back out (write-through), so the operator still sees the ~134s run instead of silence'), the two source comments that assert it (check-all.ts:13-16 'echoed straight back to the operator (so the ~134s run is not silent)' and check-all.ts:220-227 'Echo ... (write-through, so the ~134s run is not silent)'), and ADR-0056's Consequences ('the operator's live progress must be teed rather than swallowed'). Measured at Layer B: Bun.spawnSync with stdout/stderr 'pipe' blocks until the child exits and returns the complete Buffers at once (real probe: parent unblocked after 3018ms for an `echo EARLY; sleep 3; echo LATE` child, receiving 'EARLY\nLATE\n' in one piece; confirmed by bun.sh/docs/api/spawn, 'Bun.spawnSync is the blocking equivalent of Bun.spawn'). captureAndEchoSuiteOutput runs only after spawnFn returns (check-all.ts:251 then 260), so `bun run check:all` is indistinguishable from a wedged pane for the 100971ms the reviewer's own run measured on the `test` gate, then dumps ~2500 lines at once. The output is preserved, so this is not inert, but the shipped behaviour is a post-hoc replay, not a tee. The AC2 oracle passed only because it greps for the markers after the process exits, so a green oracle does not settle this. Recommended fix on merit: make the suite gate a streaming tee (async Bun.spawn, reading stdout/stderr incrementally into the shared blob while writing each chunk straight through, which makes runGates async and ripples to check-all.ts's CLI entry plus the three check-all test files). If the post-hoc replay is instead accepted as the permanent shape, then the three claims above must be corrected in the same change (source comments restated to say the blob is replayed after the gate completes, and ADR-0056's consequence sentence amended by an explicit supersession note rather than a silent rewrite), because a comment that mis-states runtime behaviour is exactly what the next worker will trust.

userStories.title: CRITICAL: US-002's in-process gate behaviour has no committed regression test.…
userStories.description: CRITICAL [test/check-all.test.ts:176]: US-002's in-process gate behaviour has no committed regression test. The only changed assertions for the two collapsed gates are structural (`expect(gate && 'run' in gate).toBe(true)` / `expect(gate && 'cmd' in gate).toBe(false)` at test/check-all.test.ts:176-182), and test/check-all-capture.test.ts covers only decodeCapturedOutput plus the onSuiteOutput hook with gate lists that contain no in-process gate. Nothing committed asserts that runGates actually threads the captured blob into gate.run (scripts/check-all.ts:332-333), that an empty blob fails both gates closed, that a below-floor blob fails coverage, or that a failing suite does not contaminate the coverage/skip-ratchet rows. Replacing the threaded blob with '', inverting a gate verdict, or making runInProcessGate a no-op leaves the whole suite green: the three full-manifest tests (test/check-all.test.ts:366, :379) already execute the real in-process gates and were observed printing 'fail coverage'/'fail skip-ratchet' while still passing, since they assert only names and lengths. The anti-inert guarantee ADR-0056 was written to secure therefore lives only in the ephemeral prd.json oracle strings, which are overwritten on the next PRD cycle. Add committed tests (empty-blob fail-closed, below-floor coverage fail, three skip-ratchet failure modes, anti-contamination) using an injected gates array of the two in-process gates.

userStories.title: WARNING: An exception thrown by an in-process gate escapes runGates and aborts…
userStories.description: WARNING [scripts/check-all.ts:284]: An exception thrown by an in-process gate escapes runGates and aborts the whole spine. executeGate calls runInProcessGate unguarded, and checkCoverage/checkSkipRatchet both do readFileSync + JSON.parse on their real budget/expectations files (scripts/check-coverage.ts:138, scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts:274). Reproduced: `runGates({ cwd: '/tmp', spawnFn: <valid-blob fake>, onResults: ... })` printed 7 ok rows then THREW 'ENOENT ... /tmp/scripts/coverage-budget.json'; the remaining 6 gates never ran and onResults never fired, so under --json no gate-results.json is written and CI's step-summary step would find no file. Before the collapse the same condition was contained in the check-coverage.ts subprocess and surfaced as a `fail coverage` row with the spine continuing. Wrap gate.run in try/catch and map a throw to { passed: false, errors: [message] }.

userStories.title: Capture the suite gate's combined output in check-all
userStories.description: As the gate spine, I need the suite gate to run `bun test --coverage` with piped stdio and expose its combined stdout+stderr as one shared blob (while still echoing that output to the operator), so that the coverage and skip-ratchet consumers can later be fed from it instead of re-running the suite.
acceptanceCriteria: Change-detection. The single suite entry in the GATES manifest is `bun test --coverage`, not plain `bun test` (issue AC2). SWEPT AGAINST MAIN 2026-08-03: prints `RED suite=bun test`, exit 0 (a real red, not an extraction failure). [oracle: bun -e "import { runGates } from './scripts/check-all.ts'; const log = new Array<string>(); runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => { log.push(c + ' ' + a.join(' ')); return { success: true, exitCode: 0 }; }) as never }); const suite = log.filter((l) => /^bun test( |$)/.test(l)); console.log(suite.length === 1 && /^bun test --coverage( |$)/.test(suite.at(0) ?? '') ? 'GREEN' : 'RED suite=' + suite.join(' | '));"]

Change-detection. The suite gate is spawned with BOTH streams piped and the captured buffers are echoed back out (write-through), so the operator still sees the ~134s run instead of silence: a fake spawn whose stdout Buffer says SENTINELOUT and whose stderr Buffer says SENTINELERR causes both markers to appear in check-all's own output. SWEPT AGAINST MAIN 2026-08-03: prints RED (main never reads result.stdout/result.stderr at all). [oracle: bun -e "import { runGates } from './scripts/check-all.ts'; runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => ({ success: true, exitCode: 0, stdout: Buffer.from('SENTINELOUT'), stderr: Buffer.from('SENTINELERR') })) as never });" > /tmp/cam488-echo.txt 2>&1; grep -q 'SENTINELOUT' /tmp/cam488-echo.txt && grep -q 'SENTINELERR' /tmp/cam488-echo.txt && echo GREEN || echo RED]

Change-detection. Exit-code fidelity survives the switch to piped stdio: when the fake spawn fails ONLY the suite invocation, the `test` row of the GateResult array is still `fail` (verdict stays `result.success && result.exitCode === 0`, never inferred from the captured text). SWEPT AGAINST MAIN 2026-08-03: prints `RED test=ok`, exit 0. [oracle: bun -e "import { runGates } from './scripts/check-all.ts'; let rows = new Array(); runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => ({ success: !a.includes('--coverage'), exitCode: a.includes('--coverage') ? 1 : 0, stdout: Buffer.from('x'), stderr: Buffer.from(' 0 pass') })) as never, onResults: (r) => { rows = r; } }); const t = rows.find((x) => x.name === 'test'); console.log(t && t.status === 'fail' ? 'GREEN' : 'RED test=' + (t ? t.status : 'missing'));"]

Change-detection. A new unit-test file `test/check-all-capture.test.ts` exists and drives the capture path with a fake spawn, asserting at minimum: (a) the shared blob is stdout-decoded text FOLLOWED BY stderr-decoded text, in that order (measured reality: `bun test --coverage` writes everything to stderr, so a stdout-only capture yields an empty blob); (b) a spawn result whose stdout/stderr are `undefined` decodes to an empty blob instead of throwing. SWEPT AGAINST MAIN 2026-08-03: `bun test test/check-all-capture.test.ts` exits 1 (no such file), so the oracle is red-on-main. [oracle: bun test test/check-all-capture.test.ts]

Invariance pin (green by construction, deliberate). Gate identity is untouched by this story: the GATES manifest still declares 14 gates with the same names in the same order. [oracle: bun test test/gates-manifest.test.ts]

The `scripts/check-all.ts` entry in scripts/file-size-budget.json (176 today, at its ceiling) is raised with the CAM-488 tracker ref recorded in the budget file's `_ref` string, and the file-size gate passes. [oracle: bun scripts/check-file-sizes.ts]

Lint passes with no new cognitive-complexity or lines-per-function violation (`noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity` max 15 and `noExcessiveLinesPerFunction` max 80 are both errors for scripts/**; extract the capture into its own helper rather than growing runGates). [oracle: bun run lint]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes:
Files: scripts/check-all.ts (SpawnFn type + runGates + new capture helper), test/check-all.test.ts (the `test gate: bun test` assertion at the per-gate block must be restated to `bun test --coverage`, and the `makeResult` fake at test/check-all.test.ts:33-43 must grow stdout/stderr Buffers), NEW test/check-all-capture.test.ts, scripts/file-size-budget.json.

MECHANISM IS PINNED, NOT AN OPEN CHOICE: the shared blob MUST derive from the spawn result's piped Buffers (`stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe'` on the suite spawn only; decode stdout then stderr and concatenate, exactly as the two existing adapters already do at check-coverage.ts:132 and check-skip-ratchet.ts:269), with live progress restored by echoing the captured buffers back to process.stdout/process.stderr after the spawn returns. Do NOT implement this as a `tee`/`pipefail` shell form: every downstream oracle in US-002 and US-003 injects the blob through the fake spawn's stdout/stderr Buffers, a shape only the piped form can produce, so a tee-based capture would strand them.

Keep the non-suite gates on inherited stdio; only the suite gate is captured. That means SpawnFn's baked-in 'inherit','inherit' generics (check-all.ts:34) must widen (e.g. to a structural `{ success, exitCode, stdout?: Buffer, stderr?: Buffer }` subset, or `SyncSubprocess<'pipe'|'inherit','pipe'|'inherit'>`); `import type { SyncSubprocess } from 'bun'` stays.

patterns.md bullets to re-read before coding (grep them, do not read the file whole): 'Oracle-friendly manifest design (US-001, CAM-59)' -- keep GATES entries as full space-separated command strings so `g(name, cmdStr)` still splits them and grep-based oracles still match; 'Migrating an injectable SpawnFn seam ... to Bun.spawnSync (US-001, CAM-308)' -- the pass/fail verdict must stay `result.success && result.exitCode === 0` (a signal-killed child reports exitCode null at runtime), and any hand-built SyncSubprocess fixture needs a fully zeroed ResourceUsage object, not a partial cast; 'Oracle-falsifiability rule (US-001, CAM-372)' at patterns.md:928 -- every assertion you add must be swept red against main first.

Bun docs (fetched this plan, see officialDocsConsulted): stdout defaults to 'pipe' but stderr defaults to 'inherit', so BOTH must be set explicitly; leave `maxBuffer` unset (it kills the child once exceeded, and the coverage table plus summary is hundreds of KB).

CAM-474 bracket rule: the oracles above are deliberately bracket-free. If you re-run them, treat exit 2 or a syntax error as an EXTRACTION failure, never as a red criterion.

userStories.title: Feed coverage and skip-ratchet from the shared blob in-process
userStories.description: As a worker or reviewer running `bun run check:all`, I need the coverage and skip-ratchet gates to reach their verdicts from the already-captured suite output instead of spawning their own consumer scripts, so that one check:all costs one suite execution instead of three while each gate keeps its own failure condition.
acceptanceCriteria: Change-detection (issue AC1). One check:all issues exactly ONE suite spawn and ZERO consumer-script spawns. SWEPT AGAINST MAIN 2026-08-03: prints `RED suite=1 consumers=2`, exit 0. [oracle: bun -e "import { runGates } from './scripts/check-all.ts'; const log = new Array<string>(); runGates({ spawnFn: ((c, a) => { log.push(c + ' ' + a.join(' ')); return { success: true, exitCode: 0 }; }) as never }); const suite = log.filter((l) => /^bun test( |$)/.test(l)).length; const cons = log.filter((l) => /check-(coverage|skip-ratchet)\.ts/.test(l)).length; console.log(suite === 1 && cons === 0 ? userStories.title: Measure the collapsed check:all and record the numbers durably
userStories.description: As the operator paying the recurring per-cycle check:all tax, I need the before/after wall-clock and per-gate durations actually measured and written into the durable pattern record, so that the collapse cannot ship inert with a green oracle and no real speedup.
acceptanceCriteria: Change-detection, value criterion (issue AC9). A real `bun scripts/check-all.ts --json` run on the branch produces a gate-results.json in which the `coverage` and `skip-ratchet` rows are each under a tenth of the `test` row (on main they are near-identical: 34511ms test vs 34381ms coverage in the recorded gate-results.json, the empirical fingerprint of the redundant run). The harness below was validated 2026-08-03 against a gate-results.json carrying main's recorded shape and printed `RED test=134000ms coverage=133800ms skip-ratchet=133900ms`. [oracle: bun scripts/check-all.ts --json; bun -e "const rows = await Bun.file('gate-results.json').json(); const d = (n) => { const r = rows.find((x) => x.name === n); return r ? r.durationMs : -1; }; const ok = d('test') > 1000 && d('coverage') > -1 && d('skip-ratchet') > -1 && d('coverage') < d('test') / 10 && d('skip-ratchet') < d('test') / 10; console.log(ok ? 'GREEN' : 'RED test=' + d('test') + 'ms coverage=' + d('coverage') + 'ms skip-ratchet=' + d('skip-ratchet') + 'ms');"]

Change-detection, durable record with a PINNED measurement shape (issue AC9). A CAM-488 bullet is appended to scripts/cam/patterns.md carrying BOTH measurements in this exact token form: `check:all before <N>s, after <N>s` and `per-gate after: test <N>ms, coverage <N>ms, skip-ratchet <N>ms`, where the before number is a real measured main-side total (not the recorded 34s sample re-quoted as if it were a fresh run) and the after numbers come from the gate-results.json of the criterion above. Both consumer scripts still run standalone and self-sufficiently, each performing its own suite execution with no check-all around it, and each still exits 0. findings.text: Layer B behavioral gate FAIL, independently reproduced at branch HEAD (064bb52b) by this reviewer in round 6. 8 recorded change-detection oracle directives print RED. Verbatim re-run: US-001 AC1 'RED suite='; US-001 AC3 'RED test=missing'; US-002 AC1 'RED suite=0 consumers=0'; US-002 AC2 'RED cov=missing suite=0 consumers=0'; US-002 AC3 'RED BAD status=missing suite=0 | BAD status=missing suite=0 | BAD status=missing suite=0'; US-002 AC4 'RED a=missing/missing/missing b=missing/missing'; US-002 AC5 'RED cov=missing sr=missing suite=0 consumers=0'; US-002 AC7 'RED keys= names='. Root cause verified in source: US-R2-001 made the spine async end to end (scripts/check-all.ts:63 SpawnFn returns a Promise; scripts/check-all.ts:407 runGates returns Promise<number>), but every one of these directives calls runGates({...}) WITHOUT await and reads its log/rows array on the very next synchronous statement, so it observes an empty array before any gate has run. Control proving the product itself is intact: the same directives rewritten with 'await runGates(...)' and an async fake spawnFn print GREEN, test/check-all-inprocess-gates.test.ts covers the same behaviour against the real manifest gates and passes, bun test is 5956 pass / 0 fail, and a real 'bun scripts/check-all.ts --json' is green on all 14 gates. This is a broken proof-of-record, not a broken feature, but these 8 criteria carry the entire anti-inert value of US-001/US-002 (one suite spawn, zero consumer spawns, exit-code fidelity, under-floor coverage fail, three skip-ratchet failure modes, anti-contamination, empty-blob fail-closed, gate identity) and read RED for the ship gate, for the next planner's red-against-main sweep, and for the next reviewer. Fix: restate the 8 directives against the async seam (await runGates(...) with an async fake spawnFn) and re-sweep them red-against-main. Include US-001 AC2 in the same restatement: it prints GREEN only incidentally. This reviewer re-captured its output and grepped it: the ONLY SENTINELOUT/SENTINELERR hit is line 17, the skip-ratchet failure message's 'Raw output (first 300 chars):' dump of the raw blob. After US-R2-001 no echo path exists for an injected fake at all (the tee lives in runStreamingSuiteGate, scripts/check-all.ts:276-298, reachable only via the default spawnFn at :392-398; runSpawnGate at :321-334 has no echo), so AC2 would stay green even if the tee were deleted entirely. Raised in rounds 3, 4 and 5; unaddressed at HEAD. Note: prd.json is write-blocked for worker-actor sessions by .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh, so this must land via a planner/reviewer/operator pass, not an implementer story.

The US-R1-001 bullet added earlier on this same branch is factually wrong at branch HEAD and will land on main as durable knowledge, and the branch's largest architectural change has no bullet at all. (a) The bullet asserts that "runSpawnGate's captureAndEchoSuiteOutput unconditionally echoes the 'test' gate's captured buffers to the REAL process.stdout/process.stderr" and prescribes wrapping such runGates calls in a withSilentStdio helper. US-R2-001 deleted that post-hoc echo. Verified independently: a repo-wide grep over *.ts and *.md for 'captureAndEchoSuiteOutput|withSilentStdio' returns exactly ONE hit, inside this bullet's own prose, so the hazard described no longer exists in that form and the guard prescribed is unimplementable. A future worker following it will either silence stdout for no reason or trust an echo behaviour that is gone. (b) grep -c 'US-R2-001, CAM-488' scripts/cam/patterns.md returns 0: US-001/US-002/US-003/US-R1-001/US-R1-002 each added a bullet, but the sync-to-async ripple across SpawnFn/runGates/runSpawnGate/executeGate plus the teeStream/runStreamingSuiteGate contract, the branch's largest change, is unrecorded. (c) While editing the same file, drop the 4 em-dashes the new CAM-488 bullets introduce; the operator's persisted-markdown convention forbids em-dash in human-readable .md. Fix is mechanical and single-file. Raised in rounds 3, 4 and 5; unaddressed at HEAD.

makeDefaultSpawnFn decides to STREAM from argv shape (cmd === 'bun' && args[0] === 'test' && args.includes('--coverage')) while runSpawnGate decides to capture and share the blob from the gate NAME (SUITE_GATE_NAME, line 329). Renaming the suite gate keeps the live tee but drops the shared blob; changing its args does the reverse. It fails closed (an empty blob fails both in-process gates, proven at Layer B by the awaited US-002 AC5 variant), so it is a trap rather than a silent pass, but keying both off one predicate would remove the divergence.

teeStream ignores the return value of sink.write(chunk), so backpressure is never awaited (no 'drain' wait). Combined with the CLI entry's process.exit(code) at line 450, still-buffered output could in principle be truncated when stdout is a pipe. Not observed in this reviewer's own piped runs, where every gate line and the full teed suite output arrived intact.

runSpawnGate awaits spawnFn without a try/catch, so a spawn throw still escapes runGates and aborts the remaining gates with no gate-results.json written, the exact failure class US-R1-002 just contained for in-process gates (runInProcessGate, line 345). Confirmed pre-existing rather than introduced here (Bun.spawnSync throws on ENOENT identically to Bun.spawn), but US-R1-002's own containment argument applies verbatim to the spawn branch.

The streaming proof asserts writeTimestamps[0] - start < 300 against a subprocess that must be spawned, scheduled and produce its first chunk. Under the repo's own check:all (where this file runs inside a full 'bun test --coverage' with 5956 tests) a 300ms first-chunk budget is a plausible flake source, even though the intent (early marker arrives before the deliberate 400ms sleep) is right. Widening the lower bound and raising the subprocess sleep proportionally would keep the same falsifying power with more headroom. Passed in this review both standalone and inside check:all's test gate.

A large share of the file-size ceiling raise (176 -> 452) is narrative comment prose re-litigating story history (lines 13-30, 52-62, 249-255, 266-274, 300-320, 385-390 each restate what a prior shape did and why it was replaced). The executable growth is cohesive and belongs here, so the raise is justified, but that history is what scripts/cam/patterns.md and the budget _ref exist to carry; trimming the superseded-shape narratives would leave the same explanatory value at a lower ceiling.

makeDefaultSpawnFn is module-private and every committed test injects a fake SpawnFn, so its pipe-vs-inherit routing predicate is never exercised by bun test. runStreamingSuiteGate itself now has real-subprocess coverage (test/check-all-streaming.test.ts) and this reviewer proved the real path live at the wire, so the residual untested surface is only the predicate; exporting it (or a single runGates run over a one-file 'test' gate with the default spawnFn) would close it.
